title: Reporting an unusual or excessive loss or disappearance of a scheduled listed chemical product
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.15, each regulated person must report to the Special Agent in Charge of the DEA Divisional Office for the area in which the regulated person making the report is located any unusual or excessive loss or disappearance of a scheduled listed chemical product under the control of the regulated person, and the regulated person responsible for reporting a loss in-transit is the supplier. Each report must, whenever possible, be made orally to the DEA Divisional Office for that area at the earliest practicable opportunity after the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances involved; written reports of losses must be filed within 15 days after the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances of the event; a report must include a description of the circumstances of the loss (in-transit, theft from premises, etc.); and the section provides a suggested format for the report.
exam_relevance: Tests the listed-chemical loss report as a duty of its own: what triggers it, who reports a loss in transit, the oral report at the earliest practicable opportunity and the written report within 15 days after the regulated person becomes aware.

numeric_facts.conditions: After the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances of the event

common_confusions: For a loss in transit the supplier is the regulated person responsible for reporting.
The 15-day period for the written report runs from when the regulated person becomes aware of the circumstances, not from the date of the loss.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1314.15 read in the eCFR, current through 2026-09-14, on 2026-09-16.
